5/ We must build the data foundry that ushers in an era of AI-ready data abundance, and not resign ourselves to data scarcity.

4/ The future of AI data in turn depends on three principles:

1. data abundance
2. frontier data
3. measurement & evaluation

data.text:
2/ Thank you to our existing investors: Y Combinator, Nat Friedman, Index Ventures, Founders Fund, Coatue, Thrive Capital, Spark Capital, Tiger Global Management, Greenoaks, and Wellington Management.

We also are excited to welcome new investors: Cisco Investments, DFJ Growth,

10/ Solving the AI data problem is really important. It's my life's work.

We're excited to make some major announcements about this next week.

For now... stay tuned!

9/ But we really need a step change here. Every major AI breakthrough over the past two decades has been driven by better and more data—dating back to the original deep neural network of AlexNet on ImageNet.

Scaling laws clearly illustrate where we're headed—we need more data!

8/ AI data is a REALLY hard problem, and there's no easy way around it.

Pure synthetic data is not our savior—synthetic data cannot push the frontiers of the models beyond current capabilities. It is a tool, not a panacea.

This is a hard AI & human-expert symbiosis problem.

7/ This is EXTRA true once you start considering all the areas of frontier research:

agents, multimodality, multilinguality, expert chain-of-thought, enterprise workflows, etc.

All of these depend on data that simply does not exist today, and we require the means of production.

6/ Regardless, this points to what we might need to expect for future advancement too:

Pushing further on post-training, which necessitates abundant frontier data.

Forward progress might be fully bottlenecked on post-training data abundance.

5/ In fact, most of the differences between the top models today (Claude 3, Llama3, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5) seem to be driven entirely by post-training, not pre-training.

This might be because of supply chain problems in pre-training—getting compute stood up + data scarcity.

4/ The massive eval gains of GPT-4o, which are staggering, seem to be nearly entirely driven by great POST-TRAINING.

Comparing GPT-4 at launch vs GPT 4o, which are night-and-day, shows the power of great post-training with great data.

3/ Regardless, the level of convergence is fascinating—the similarity between 4o and Astra, Veo and Sora, etc. Both labs seem to be following relatively similar technical trajectories.

IMO, it's better for the industry for divergence rather than convergence. Alas...

2/ In many ways, Gemini 1.5 Flash was the gem of Google's announcements. A 1M-context small model with Flash performance is incredible.

OpenAI now has the best large model with GPT-4o, and Google has the best small model with Gemini 1.5 Flash.

The competition is on.

1/ Some thoughts on the recent OpenAI and Google announcements, and what it indicates about what's next in AI.

Hint: post-training is REALLY important...

We’re excited to announce that Suno has raised $125 million to build a future where anyone can make music, and where technology amplifies our most precious resource: human creativity. We will use this funding to accelerate product development and grow our world-class team of music makers, music lovers and technologists.

Our community of musicians deserves the very best tools, and building the very best tools requires the very best talent — not just technological expertise, but a genuine love of music. If you want to be part of this journey and help shape the future of music, join us here:  https://t.co/8RKlWIR6v8

Most importantly, thank you to our amazing community. We’ve been heads-down, hard at work on a number of major updates. We think you’re going to love them, and we look forward to sharing more with you soon!

To read our full announcement, visit our blog: https://t.co/HvYbaO4LHy
